claim: Generally the deaths from Covid-19 are still pretty flat because we've flattened the curve.
justification: High-confidence evidence (e.g., confidence=0.90) indicates that U.S. COVID-19 death rates had plateaued by October 21, 2020, supporting the 'flat' part of the claim. However, equally high-confidence evidence (confidence=0.90) from Dr. Fauci and other sources explains that 'flattening the curve' does not necessarily lead to flat death trends over extended periods, refuting the causal link asserted in the claim. Additionally, evidence suggests new cases were rising at the time, contradicting the idea that the curve was successfully flattened. Therefore, the claim as a whole is refuted.
